newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GDP pushes NZ dollar lower, debt reaction muted.
newsitem.headline: GDP pushes NZ dollar lower, debt reaction muted.

text.p: Softer than forecast New Zealand Gross Domestic Product data on Monday pushed the Kiwi dollar lower and more than justified the central bank's 100-point easing of monetary policy last Friday, dealers said.
The 0.5 percent fall in GDP for the March quarter was lower than market expectations of a 0.1 percent fall and significantly off the central bank's projection of a 0.3 percent rise.

Just as the RBNZ's easing signal last week has found expression mainly in a lower currency, reaction to the weak GDP indicator was once again felt mostly in the Kiwi, which shed over a quarter of a cent against the greenback.

"That number again emphasises the clear fact that the economy is struggling and provides further evidence that the 100 basis point sanctioning that we got from the Reserve Bank's monetary policy statement last week is more than justified," said a chief dealer at a Wellington bank.
"Clearly it's prompted some selling in the Kiwi. U.S.-based customers have predominantly been the major sellers," he said.
The Kiwi fell to US$0.6779/86 within an hour and a half of the GDP release from about 0.6797 prior.
Reaction to the data in the debt market, however, was relatively muted.
"Certainly it rallied down a couple of points on its release, but it's subsequently given back most of that and is now only a point lower across the curve," said a dealer.
"I think the market was anticipating a reasonably weak (GDP) outcome."
The 90-day bank bill yield rallied about three points initially but quickly returned to its opening level of 6.92 percent. Bond yields were similarly unruffled.
"The risk is, from the Reserve Bank's perspective, that the market will try to take conditions lower over time," the dealer said.
"It will be an interesting few weeks because every partial indicator that comes out will be looked at more closely than it probably has been in the past."
